decisions.original_gate_note: failed only because of the extra conjunct requiring a significant win over the crude estimator on the pooled side

limits: Moments rather than REML, and tau-squared is truncated at zero which affects lambda.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI.

the_primary_question_answered_yes.question: does shrinkage make the pathway prior beat an uninformed baseline at the drug level?
the_primary_question_answered_yes.reading: shrinkage turns a negative-R2 estimator into a positive one on the library side, doubles R2 on the anchor side, and on the pooled side it beats the grand mean significantly

my_gate_was_wrong_again.what_i_required: H352 demanded both that shrunk beat the grand mean AND that it beat the crude estimator
my_gate_was_wrong_again.why_the_second_conjunct_is_not_the_quest: the question was whether shrinkage makes the prior usable, which is exactly the comparison against an uninformed baseline. Beating the crude estimator is a separate and stricter demand, and on the pooled side there is little room because crude was already respectable there (R2 0.151).
my_gate_was_wrong_again.count: fifth gate mismatch, after R103, R107, R112 and R142, all of the same family: adding a conjunct that does not answer the question being asked

the_quantitative_prior_strength.reading: with tau-squared at about 0.4 times sigma-squared, roughly 28 percent of the drug-level variance in mean response lies between pathways. That is the quantity the annotation is worth, and it is why shrinkage is needed: five drugs per group cannot estimate a group mean without borrowing strength.

the_mechanism_chain_is_closed.step_1: pathway membership is associated with drug behaviour (C110, permutation p 0.000)
the_mechanism_chain_is_closed.step_2: a crude group mean cannot exploit that because groups average five drugs (C110)
the_mechanism_chain_is_closed.step_3: a shrunk estimator can: it beats the uninformed baseline significantly, and on the anchor side it beats the crude estimator too (C111)
the_mechanism_chain_is_closed.step_4: at the model level the same shrinkage is what ridge performs, which is why the substitution effect appears there (C106)
the_mechanism_chain_is_closed.so: the prior is real, it is exploitable only with borrowing of strength, and the model does that borrowing automatically
